concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-braintree-transaction-submit-for-partial-settlement-node]] - Node.js multiple partial settlement against one parent authorization, with separate child transactions and child-only refund restrictions, plus a preserved payment-method availability conflict and damaged lifecycle-status rendering
warnings: Preserve the availability conflict. Primary evidence: `raw/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/submit-for-partial-settlement/node-2026-09-16.md`, lines 16-17: `Multiple partial settlements are only available for PayPal and Venmo transactions.` Supporting evidence: `raw/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/submit-for-settlement/node-2026-09-16.md`, line 32: `If you want to settle for an amount that is different from the total authorization amount, you can specify the amount to settle. If you do not specify, the entire amount will be settled. You can only submit for settlement for an amount that is less than the total authorization amount one time. To submit more than once, you will need to use multiple partial settlements; this method is available for[PayPal](/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/submit-for-partial-settlement)and[Venmo](/braintree/docs/guides/venmo/submit-for-partial-settlement)transactions, and[some credit card transactions](/braintree/docs/guides/credit-cards/submit-for-partial-settlement)for select merchants.` Do not state a universal eligibility rule.
Do not reconstruct the method omitted after `Authorize the entire order amount using.` or any missing parent/child lifecycle state and transition names in the damaged rendering.
Keep the central behavior scoped to multiple partial settlement: one parent authorization and a separate child transaction for each settled portion.
Keep refunds scoped to child transactions, capped by the amount settled on that child, and conditioned on full settlement; the required rendered state name is unavailable.
